name: Russian Twist
description: The Russian twist is a rotational core exercise performed in a seated position with the torso leaned back at an angle. The lifter rotates the torso side to side, training the obliques and transverse abdominis in a rotational pattern. It can be performed with bodyweight, a weight plate, or a medicine ball.

execution.starting_position: Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet flat or slightly elevated. Lean back until the torso is at approximately 45 degrees from the floor. Hold a weight or clasp hands together in front of the chest.
execution.setup_instructions: Feet can be anchored for beginners. Advanced lifters can elevate the feet for greater difficulty.
steps: Rotate the torso to one side, bringing the hands or weight toward the floor beside the hip.
Rotate back through center and to the other side.
One rotation to each side counts as one complete repetition.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on each rotation. Breathe rhythmically.
common_mistakes: Rotating with the arms only — the rotation must come from the torso
Relaxing the core during the movement
safety_considerations: If lower back discomfort occurs, reduce the torso lean angle
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Rotate as far as the torso allows without losing the leaned-back position.
coaching_cues: Let your ribs lead the rotation — not your arms
Keep the chest up and spine long throughout
